column1: # title: ENG-205 Sir Gawain Part 1 — 4 Main Ideas

column2: During King Arthur's New Year feast at Camelot, a giant green knight rides in and dares any knight to strike him with an axe and take the same blow next year.

column1: 2. Gawain takes the swing for Arthur
column2: When no knight answers and the Green Knight mocks the Round Table, Arthur grabs the axe himself, so his nephew Gawain takes his place and chops off the Green Knight's head.
Instead of dying, the Green Knight picks up his own head and orders Gawain to find him at the Green Chapel next New Year's Day "or be called a coward forever."
Because Gawain promised to take the return blow, he rides off alone after All Saints' Day, carrying a shield with the pentangle, the "endless knot" standing for his faithfulness.
Since nobody knows where the Green Chapel is, Gawain wanders through freezing wilderness fighting beasts and giants, until he prays to Mary on Christmas Eve and a castle appears.
The castle's lord, Bertilak, says the Green Chapel is two miles away, so Gawain stays until New Year's and agrees to trade whatever he gains daily for Bertilak's hunting catch.
